texts.cf_intro: This is the only application file. Node.js, Python and Wrangler are not required on the user's computer.
texts.security: SECURITY: create every value listed below as type Secret. Never paste tokens or service-account JSON into worker.js, chat messages, screenshots or a public repository.
texts.botfather: In Telegram, open the verified @BotFather, run /newbot, follow its prompts and copy the bot token. Keep the token private. Bot name, description and /setcommands are optional and can also be configured in BotFather.
texts.create_steps: Open Cloudflare Dashboard > Workers & Pages > Create application > Create Worker. Deploy the starter Worker once, open it and choose Edit Code. Open worker.js on your computer, copy all of it, replace all starter code in the Cloudflare editor, then select Deploy. If the editor offers file import, worker.js may be imported instead.
texts.secret_steps: Open the Worker > Settings > Variables and Secrets > Add. For EACH name below choose Secret, paste the value, and save/deploy the new version. Names are case-sensitive. Do not add quotation marks unless they are part of the value.
texts.setup_steps: After deployment copy the public https://...workers.dev address. Open that address with /setup appended, for example https://your-worker.workers.dev/setup. Enter the exact SETUP_SECRET value and select Register webhook. The Worker sends setWebhook to Telegram itself; BOT_TOKEN never enters the browser URL. A successful page shows ok=true and the registered HTTPS webhook address.
texts.manual: What setWebhook does: it sends url=<Worker URL + Telegram path>, secret_token=<WEBHOOK_SECRET>, allowed_updates from this project, and drop_pending_updates=false to https://api.telegram.org/bot<BOT_TOKEN>/setWebhook. Telegram then POSTs updates to the Worker and includes WEBHOOK_SECRET in the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header. The Worker rejects requests without the matching header.
texts.check: Use Check webhook on /setup. The result of getWebhookInfo must show the same URL and no last_error_message. Then open the bot in Telegram and send /start. No further Telegram-side setup is required for a private chat bot.
texts.update: TO UPDATE: edit the project in TRIGRIX Studio, export a new worker.js, replace all code in Edit Code and deploy. Secrets remain in Cloudflare and must not be copied into the file. Re-run /setup only if the Worker URL, Telegram path, BOT_TOKEN or WEBHOOK_SECRET changed.
texts.trouble: TROUBLESHOOTING: 401/403 means a missing or mismatched Secret; Telegram getWebhookInfo reports delivery errors; Cloudflare Logs shows runtime errors. Confirm exact variable names, deploy after every Secret change, and ensure the Worker URL is public HTTPS. If /start does nothing, register the webhook again and check getWebhookInfo.
texts.firebase: FIREBASE/FIRESTORE: enable Firestore in the Firebase project, create a service account key in Google Cloud IAM, download its JSON, compact it to one line and paste the complete JSON as the FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON Secret. Set the project/database/collection in TRIGRIX Studio before export. Never place the JSON key in worker.js.
texts.other: OTHER SERVICES: API keys, CRM tokens, Meta/Viber tokens, email credentials and verification secrets must also be Cloudflare Secrets. Public IDs may technically be Variables, but using Secret for the whole generated list is the safest and simplest procedure. Register each enabled provider's webhook with the Worker URL plus the path shown below.
texts.docker_intro: This folder is a standalone application. TRIGRIX Studio is not required on the server.
texts.docker_install: Install Docker Desktop on Windows/macOS, or Docker Engine with the Compose plugin on Linux. Start Docker and wait until it reports that the engine is running. Open a terminal IN THIS EXPORTED FOLDER, the folder that contains compose.yaml and .env.example.
texts.docker_env: Copy .env.example to a new file named exactly .env. On Windows you may copy it in Explorer; in PowerShell use Copy-Item .env.example .env. On macOS/Linux use cp .env.example .env. Open .env in a text editor and put each value after NAME=. Do not add spaces around = and do not rename variables.
texts.docker_security: The .env file contains secrets. Never send it to anyone, commit it to Git, put it in a public repository, screenshot it or copy its values into compose.yaml. Only .env.example is safe to share because it has no values.
texts.docker_firebase: For FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, enable Firestore, create and download a service-account JSON key, convert the JSON to one line, and use FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON='{type:service_account,...}' in .env. Keep the literal \n escapes inside private_key; do not insert real line breaks.
texts.docker_run: Run docker compose up -d --build. Wait for completion, then run docker compose ps; the service must be Up/running. View live logs with docker compose logs -f. Press Ctrl+C to leave logs without stopping the bot. Test the Telegram bot with /start.
texts.docker_manage: Restart: docker compose restart. Rebuild after a new export: docker compose up -d --build. Stop: docker compose stop. Stop and remove the container: docker compose down. These commands must be run from the same exported folder.
texts.docker_telegram: Telegram uses long polling in Docker, so setWebhook is not needed. On startup the container removes an old webhook and begins polling. The server must have continuous Internet access. For groups/channels, add the bot and grant the required permissions in Telegram.
texts.docker_webhooks: For non-Telegram channels, expose port 8080, place an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it, and register https://YOUR-DOMAIN plus the generated channel path with the provider. Do not expose an unencrypted HTTP webhook to the Internet.
texts.docker_trouble: If the container exits, run docker compose logs --tail=200. Typical causes are an empty BOT_TOKEN, a misspelled variable, invalid JSON in FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON, Docker not running, or blocked outbound Internet. After changing .env run docker compose up -d --force-recreate.
texts.commands: Telegram commands configured in this project
texts.setup_secret: A new random phrase of at least 24 characters, used only to protect /setup

email_binding: Cloudflare Send Email binding (this is a resource, not a variable): open Worker > Settings > Bindings > Add > Send Email, set the binding name to {binding}, and allow only these verified destinations: {recipients}.

setup_ui.title: Telegram webhook setup
setup_ui.safe: The token stays inside Cloudflare Secrets.
setup_ui.invalid_webhook_secret: WEBHOOK_SECRET must contain only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or - and be 1–256 characters.
